summary: Follow-up on Dec 20 Sable outage. Reviewed root cause (autoscaler race + KV cache corruption during failover), temporary mitigations applied, and timeline for permanent fixes and reliability improvements. Agreed next steps and owners.
transcript: 00:00 Lena Park: Thanks everyone for joining, we'll keep this tight, 30 minutes to review the postmortem and confirm next steps
00:18 Rajiv Mehta: Thanks Lena. We appreciate Redwood jumping on this, obviously the outage on Dec 20 hit a few of our pipelines hard
00:27 Miguel Ortega: Yeah hi all, Miguel here. Quick agenda recap what happened, what we shipped as a hotfix, and the longer term remediation plan
00:40 Hannah Lee: Quick note I uploaded the logs and spans to the shared folder, you should have the trace ids in the deck link
00:50 Priya Shah: I also added the customer impact spreadsheet to the doc, estimated cost impact and downtime windows per environment
01:05 Tom Wu: For context, we saw a surge in tail latency followed by cascading backend errors, right? Hannah correct me if i'm wrong

01:17 Hannah Lee: Yes, the sequence was high-concurrency burst hitting our dedicated pool, autoscaler triggered several node additions, and during the scaling window the KV cache ended up with partial shards leading to invalid cache lookups

01:35 Miguel Ortega: To be specific an autoscaler race condition + an edge case in the KV cache reconciliation path caused corrupted in-memory cache descriptors. On failover those descriptors caused some requests to return 5xx and then the health checks tripped, which made the control plane start more evictions, exacerbating the problem
02:05 Rajiv Mehta: Was there a single point of failure? We thought the control plane was redundant

02:12 Miguel Ortega: Control plane is redundant, but the interaction between the older autoscaler shim and the newer KV eviction logic wasn't exercised in our integration tests rare timing window. So not single SPOF in infra, but an emergent failure mode
02:35 Lena Park: Can you summarize what immediate mitigations we applied on Dec 20?

02:41 Miguel Ortega: Sure we rolled out hotfix v2.1.3 which adds a defensive check during KV reconciliation, introduced a short circuit for corrupted descriptors, and temporarily increased healthcheck thresholds to avoid aggressive evictions. We also rolled back a recent autoscaler tweak in the dedicated pool config
03:05 Hannah Lee: Those hotfixes stabilized the pool after about 22 minutes, we saw error rates drop back to baseline within ~30 minutes of the fix
03:18 Tom Wu: Good, but what about data consistency? Any user data lost?

03:24 Miguel Ortega: No persistent user data was lost. The corrupt state was in-memory KV cache only, and we had a fallback to source-of-truth requests which served the correct responses, albeit slower. The main impact was increased latency and some 5xx for a subset of requests during the window
03:45 Rajiv Mehta: We were also concerned about failover across regions our traffic moved to us-east and we saw about 20% higher p99 latency there
03:56 Miguel Ortega: Right, there was partial region saturation because traffic shifted. As part of remediation we propose better cross-region routing throttles and capacity reservations
04:12 Priya Shah: From CS side we logged all affected customers and contacted SLAs; Sable's incident was classified Sev2 and prioritized
04:25 Tom Wu: Can we get details on the test coverage gap? You mentioned integration tests didn't hit this path

04:32 Miguel Ortega: The issue arises on a specific timing: node join + concurrent heavy KV updates + autoscaler decision loop overlapping with reconcilers. Our current CI has synthetic scaling tests but not enough fuzzing at that interplay. We need a fuzzed integration test harness that simulates jittered scaling events
04:58 Hannah Lee: Ok, that makes sense. For our side, we'll send you the specific load profile we hit in prod so you can replicate locally

05:05 Miguel Ortega: Perfect, those traces will help. Planned permanent fixes: 1) patch the KV reconciliation to be idempotent, 2) harden autoscaler logic and add leader election guard for the decision loop, 3) add fleXible canary and throttling defaults for cross-region failover
05:30 Rajiv Mehta: Timeline?

05:33 Miguel Ortega: We're estimating a code fix for KV + autoscaler hardening by 2027-01-12, internal testing the week after, and a staged rollout with canary monitors through Jan 20. We'll prioritize this on the inference runtime backlog and allocate an on-call SE to oversee the rollout
05:52 Priya Shah: In the meantime, what operational mitigations should Sable adopt?

06:00 Miguel Ortega: Immediate recommendations: set autoscaler conservative thresholds, enable prefix KV cache warmup on cold start, and configure circuit breakers so requests hit fallback path earlier if errors spike we'll provide concrete config snippets
06:18 Hannah Lee: We'll take those changes to staging then to prod. Also want to request increased alerting granularity for KV reconciliation failures
06:28 Miguel Ortega: We'll add a dedicated metric and an alert runbook entry the runbook will include exact thresholds and a rollback play
06:38 Lena Park: Any compliance/audit concerns raised by the incident? Customers asked about logs and audit trails
06:44 Priya Shah: Redwood committed to share redact-friendly audit logs and SOC2 controls relevant to incident response I'll attach the security docs link
06:55 Rajiv Mehta: We may need KMS key rotation guidance as part of the postmortem. Not directly related but customers ask
07:02 Miguel Ortega: We'll include KMS/HSM integration notes in the security appendix of the postmortem doc
07:12 Tom Wu: On the question of pricing Sable consumed burst capacity during the incident. Can Redwood provide a credit or a short-term reserved bump?
07:22 Lena Park: Yes, we'll propose a compensatory credit for excess burst usage during the outage window I'll send the note after the call
07:30 Hannah Lee: Appreciated. One more technical clarification you mentioned fallback to source-of-truth was slower, did that cause request timeouts downstream?
07:40 Miguel Ortega: A small subset did hit downstream timeouts; we have traces. We'll analyze which external calls timed out and include recommendations for client-side retry/backoff
07:52 Priya Shah: Ok let's recap next steps and owners

07:56 Lena Park: Recap Miguel to ship hotfix and runbench and share binaries/configs (due 12/23), Miguel+SE to add fuzzed integration tests (due 1/12), Priya to send security docs and credits note (due 12/23), Hannah to share traces and validate staging configs (due 12/24), follow-up meeting 2027-01-05 does everyone agree?
08:20 Rajiv Mehta: Agreed
08:23 Tom Wu: Agreed
08:25 Hannah Lee: Agreed
08:28 Miguel Ortega: One small ask can Sable let us run a controlled chaos test in staging next week to validate reconciler behavior?
08:36 Hannah Lee: Yes we can open a window for that, we'll coordinate with your team
08:40 Lena Park: Great. We'll circulate the postmortem doc and runbook by tomorrow. Anything else from Sable?
08:47 Rajiv Mehta: No, thanks again. Please highlight any decisions that affect SLAs
08:52 Priya Shah: We'll mark SLA-impacting items in the doc and follow up
08:57 Lena Park: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with a calendar invite for Jan 5 and share the docs. Meeting adjourned.
